items.note: The page gives the chirp formula for QF_t as a linked result, as the assignment asks, then derives the cancellation RF^+_s[(RF_s u)(RF_s v)] = (u*v)/S^2 by the paper's route: R_c conjugation, tensoring, R commuting with pointwise products, and the two normalizations. It also notes that conjugation gives RF^+_s.

items.note: This is derived on another page. Here it is correctly stated with a link: 'with a_j=exp(-pi i sum_i s_i j_i^2/t_i), QF_t u = abar.(a*(abar.u))/T'. The page does not mention that a is periodic, though it does say each t_i is even.

The page writes out (F_q^+R_c z)_j = (1/q) sum_k z_{ck} e^{2pi i kj/q} = (1/q) sum_h z_h e^{2pi i h c^{-1} j/q} = (R_c^{-1}F_q^+ z)_j, justifying the substitution with 'runs once over all residues because c is a unit'. It then names R as the tensor product of the R_{t_i}, with t_i a unit mod s_i, to get F^+_s R = R^{-1}F^+_s and RF^+_s R = F^+_s. This matches the paper, and the q=5, c=3 example is correct.

The page uses (RF_s u).(RF_s v) = R(F_s u . F_s v) 'by the identity just shown' to reach F^+_s(F_s u . F_s v). It then applies F_s(u*v) = S(F_s u).(F_s v) and F^+_s F_s = I/S to obtain (1/S)F^+_s F_s(u*v) = (u*v)/S^2, exactly as the paper does.
